evidence:
Every plural/universal ask in the brief and rules is graded over the whole collection, and every 'unchanged'/'nothing changes' guard is scoped so that legitimate side effects of the same operation are not penalised. Instances checked (all of them):
(1) All-or-none bulk move (hireops_rules.md 'Every card must satisfy all the rules... If any card fails, none of them moves'): hro_bulk_all_or_none tests BOTH the offender first in board order (Z with V, B(6)) and last-but-selected-first (V with W, B(10a)), UI and replay, 'Fails if any card of a refused set moves'; hro_bulk_places counts places for the whole 3-card set; hro_bulk_move 'Fails if ... only some move' and checks the full landing order Y, W, X and A2, V.
(2) Undo 'puts every card of that move back': hro_undo_restores checks all three cards and the full Applied order 'Y, W, X, Z, A2' plus V staying, with an independent-context readback. Undo refusal conditions (moved / re-ordered / rejected since) are each exercised in hro_undo_conflict (B(11), B(14), B(15)); 'goes ahead or partly applies' fails.
(3) Undo 'unchanged' guard vs legitimate side effects: rules say 'Adding a note does not count as a change'; B(12) deliberately adds a note to A2 and has Mei re-order a DIFFERENT card (Y) and requires the undo to go ahead ('neither a note nor a change to another card counts'). Traced the board: at B(12) Screen reads Y, W, X, Z, A2, so Y (top) can only move down one place, which never displaces A2. Golden src/index.js:312 bumps version only for the moved card and writeColumn (index.js:200) renumbers positions without a version bump; index.js:354 compares only the moved cards' versions, consistent with the criterion. Scripted golden observation 'undo ignores other cards, is blocked by a reject' passed (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json; index hashes re-verified).
(4) Activity (rules sec 4 'Every job opening, added candidate, move, rejection, reopening, re-ordering and undo is recorded'): hro_activity requires 'every successful board action performed on J1 and J2 before A, by any account used', 'each card of every single and multi-card move', 'every undo', and a filter that 'shows all of that job's lines and only those'; it accepts one line naming every card of a multi-card move (conforming alternative not punished). hro_activity_refusals: 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line' (whole set).
(5) Role/anonymous refusal lists: hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_late_stages, hro_thread_access, hro_job_open each require every enumerated request/value ('each refused', 'Fails if any of these') with a same-kind control; functional prompt.md line 17 requires fresh versions so a stale-version 409 cannot masquerade as the role refusal; hro_refusal_status grades the status of all replays in R/T/C and accepts 404 for candidate requests naming another's application (rules sec 1), so a conforming app is not failed.
(6) Candidate privacy ('Nothing a candidate's browser receives'): hro_candidate_private covers 'no response a candidate page receives', and protocol K requires capturing every request/response including SSE/websocket payloads while Tomas's card is rejected and reopened; board/Activity replays may be 'refused or answered with only that candidate's own data' (conforming alternative allowed).
(7) Paging: hro_thread_earlier 'adds 30 at a time ... until none remain' (whole history); hro_thread_latest checks exactly the most recent 30.
(8) Exactly-one: gate hro_gate_shared requires 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' (catches duplicate writes). hro_unread_counts 'rises by exactly two' is safe because tests/test.sh run_suite uses rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1, so no other trial injects messages mid-window.
(9) Live-update preservation guards (rules sec 5 list: typed text, focus, open card, open conversation, scroll): hro_pol_live_board has a DIFFERENT card moved (so the open card's own movement is not a legitimate side effect being punished) and fails only on scroll 'reset', not on layout reflow; hro_pol_live_thread expects the view to stay at newest showing Noor's message (auto-scroll at bottom is required behaviour, not penalised).
(10) Refused actions 'change nothing': functional prompt.md line 19 scopes it to cards, order, messages and notes, and deducts Activity side effects only in hro_activity_refusals; positive controls' own changes are explicitly controls.
(11) hro_restart compares jobs, order per stage, notes, messages, unread counts and activity after a real restart_app; session loss is accommodated ('a fresh sign-in').
Minor P3 observations (no false score expected; recorded for the owner, not defects): (a) hro_candidate_view lists all six candidate wordings but protocol K only drives Application received / In review / Interviewing / Not moving forward (seed: no candidate-account card in Offer or Hired; K moves Tomas through two stages plus reject/reopen). Offer/Hired candidate labels equal the stage names, so the unobserved pair carries negligible risk. (b) hro_reopen 'after reopening the reason is gone' is phrased against the card ('keeps its reason'); the old rejection Activity line legitimately persists (rules sec 4 'Entries are never edited'), and should not be read as the card keeping its reason. (c) hro_restart 'unread counts unchanged' could be disturbed only if the judge opened a conversation with unread messages between recording and comparing; at D Rafael has already opened both of 'your conversations' in U, so their counts are 0 and the guard does not bite.
Plausible broken apps that could pass: refusing only the offending card of a bulk set but moving the rest -> caught by B(6)/B(10a) both orderings; undo restoring only the first card of a bulk move -> caught by full Y, W, X, Z, A2 readback; Activity recording only the first card of a bulk move -> caught by 'each card of every ... multi-card move'. Conforming alternatives that could fail: one Activity line per multi-card move -> explicitly accepted; renumbering sibling positions on reorder -> B(12) uses the top card's one-place move so A2 is untouched; 404 vs 403 for candidates -> accepted.
